name: Greece

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 10372335 inhabitants, recorded as 10.372 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Greek, in the transversal venues pass. One unit, one house, against an opening estimate of 1.5 produced with no research. Greece is the country where this indicator measures least, and the ministry says so itself. The national inventory of intangible cultural heritage carries a dossier on the shadow theatre, Karagiozis, filed by the Ministry of Culture, and it describes where the form is played: a permanent shadow-theatre venue has the specifications of any theatre, box office, foyer, equipped stage, and performances are also given in every space where a performance can be given at all — squares, car parks, yards, waste ground, and indoors in theatres, cinemas, clubs, cafés, schools and houses. The same dossier lists the institutions holding the form and every one of them is a museum, an archive or a collection: the Spathario museum of the municipality of Marousi, the Spyropouleio, the Charidimos museum inside the City of Athens's Melina cultural centre, the folklore museums of Ilion and Stemnitsa, the municipal gallery of Patras. Under the ruling of this repository a museum that programmes shows is not a venue of diffusion and creation, so none of them counts. And the safeguarding measures proposed by the national association of shadow theatre artists themselves end with a request for the creation of permanent stages in Athens and the regions — which is a first-party statement, in a ministry document, that they do not exist. What is counted is Πράσσειν Άλογα, the visual puppet theatre working since 1997, which holds its own place, the Κουκλόσπιτο at Β. Βουλγαροκτόνου 60 in Neapoli, Athens, where it shows performances, keeps a permanent exhibition of the puppets of its earlier productions and runs its seminars and workshops, and which names the Ministry of Culture, the Ministry of Education, the Region of Attica and the Institute of Educational Policy as its backers on its own pages. That is the same evidentiary standard on which LILARUM was counted in Vienna: funders declared by the venue, not read in an award decision. Two candidates are left out, and they are the two that show where the line falls. The Δημοτικό Θέατρο Σκιών Παλαιού Φαλήρου, in the Floisvos park on the seafront, is a municipal venue given over entirely to shadow theatre, and Tassos Konstas plays there from 1 July 2026, Wednesday to Sunday at half past eight, seven euros a ticket, as he has done for fifteen summers. It is left out under the clause that excludes a hall hosting a visiting company's series: the venue is the municipality's, but the puppetry is Konstas's own company's, brought in and taken away, which is the shape that decided Lahnstein in Germany. The reading is refutable and the whole disagreement is worth having: if the municipality is shown to programme and take responsibility for the season rather than to lend a stage, this counts and Greece is 2. The other is the Θέατρο της Κούκλας in Kato Patisia, at Ψαρουδάκη 34, a small puppet theatre in its own hall made by Takis and Mina Sarri in 1978, which the Athens listings now show with no performances at all; it is left out because nothing readable says it still plays, not because it fails the denominator. The upper bound of 3 holds both. Nothing here should be read as a measure of the activity: Greece has a shadow theatre inscribed on the national inventory of intangible heritage, a new generation of karagiozopaiktes entering the trade, and annual festivals in Athens at the Spathario museum, on Strefi hill and in Nea Ionia, and it has almost no walls. That is exactly the bias this indicator carries and cannot correct.

venues_list.authority: Υπουργείο Πολιτισμού, Υπουργείο Παιδείας, Περιφέρεια Αττικής and the Institute of Educational Policy, named as backers by the theatre itself; no award decision opened

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. The Department of Theatre Studies at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens covers theatre from bachelor's to postdoctoral level, but as a scholarly discipline, with no puppetry stream. The only occurrences of kouklotheatro identified are individual courses: one in the department of early childhood education, and an open course introducing puppetry. A puppetry course inside a preschool pedagogy curriculum does not satisfy a denominator requiring specialised higher education in puppetry arts. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1: the Greek drama schools accredited by the culture ministry were not checked one by one. Estimate, resting on search summaries.
